Business man |TV actor =[[Judson Mills]] }} '''Stephen "Steve" Winthrop''' is a character who appears in the second episode of the second season in the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]]. ==Background== Prior to the [[Great War]], Stephen Winthrop was successful man with a family. He used this success to purchase a "premium elite plus" package from the [[Vault-Tec Corporation]] that ensured him [[Cryonics|cryonic]] suspension until [[Reclamation Day (event)|Reclamation Day]]; however, he did not purchase the same for his family, which he abandoned the day of the Great War. ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===[[The Golden Rule]]=== Stephen Winthrop is thawed from his cryopod by [[Hank MacLean]] to test the [[brain-computer interface chip]] as [[Mouse|mice]] were imperfect test subjects. Before he wakes, MacLean attaches one of the chips to the back of Winthrop's neck. After attaching the chip, he is taken to another room. Winthrop begins to fully wake from the thawing still groggy sitting at a table across from MacLean who asks if his vision is fuzzy while pouring [[champagne]]. Winthrop asks who he is, MacLean answers while the brain-computer chip causes him pangs of pain. Winthrop then asks if it is Reclamation Day. MacLean lies that it is but "not quite how they thought it would be" before explaining the experiments he has been conducting on mice. Winthrop interjects that he signed up for the premium elite plus package and that there was a mistake. MacLean asks if he read the fine print and Winthrop answers yes. MacLean dodges the answer and begins to explain how much has changed since Winthrop entered his cryonic stasis, but is concerned about how much has stayed the same and the "old habits" of humanity. MacLean leads Winthrop's hands into a restraining device attached to the table. MacLean tells Winthrop that on his file he had a family but only bought a ticket for himself as he turns on a control device for the brain-computer chip. Winthrop explains that it was expensive. MacLean disapproves of his answer saying "you can't put a price on family" and cites the advertisements about its importance to Vault-Tec and how it's the first building block of civilization. Winthrop asks what MacLean is doing with the device he just turned on. MacLean answers he is improving a piece of "out dated" technology as he dials up a knob on the device. Winthrop begins to go wide eyed and shaking from the device in his neck. His teeth begin chattering before his head explodes like the mice MacLean experimented on before. ==Appearances== Stephen Winthrop appears only {{In|FOTV}}. {{FOTV appearances|10=202}} {{Navbox characters FOTV}} [[Category:Fallout TV series human characters]] [[ru:Стивен Уинтроп]]
